insights.summary: wordpress.org scores 78 out of 100 (C). 0 checks fail now, 26 are at risk, and 30 pass. Fix first: 100 images have no alt attribute.

findings.title: 100 images have no alt attribute
findings.evidence: On /, /showcase/, /plugins/, /themes/ and 6 more.
findings.fix: Describe informative images. Give decorative ones alt="".

findings.title: No content security policy
findings.evidence: content-security-policy was absent on the start page. Missing on all 20 pages read. Injected scripts are not limited by the browser.
findings.fix: Start with the Report-Only policy in the fix kit, watch the reports for a week, then enforce it.

findings.title: Tracking starts on load and no banner asks first
findings.evidence: No cookie banner appeared. Before any choice, Chromium from an EU address (Belgium) saw Google Analytics (2 requests), Google Ads (1 request), and cookies _ga, _ga_CG6GJ50G8J.
findings.fix: Hold every tag until consent, or set Google Consent Mode v2 defaults to denied before any tag loads. Block third-party embeds until the visitor agrees.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options is not sent
findings.evidence: Browsers may guess a file's type and run it as script. Missing on all 20 pages read.
findings.fix: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy is not sent
findings.evidence: Browsers fall back to their default. An explicit policy keeps full URLs from leaking to other sites. Missing on all 20 pages read.
findings.fix: Send Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy is not sent
findings.evidence: Embedded content can ask for the camera, microphone, or location. Missing on all 20 pages read.
findings.fix: Send Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=().

findings.title: Embedded frames have no title
findings.evidence: On /, /showcase/, /plugins/ and 17 more.
findings.fix: Add title="…" to each iframe.

findings.title: 6 pages have no meta description
findings.evidence: /news/, /support/forums/, /photos/, /five-for-the-future/ and 2 more. Google and AI answers then write their own snippet from whatever text they find.
findings.fix: Write a 50 to 160 character description for each page that says what a reader gets.

findings.title: 12 indexable pages are missing from the sitemap
findings.evidence: /showcase/, /plugins/, /themes/, /news/ and 8 more.
findings.fix: Add them to the sitemap or regenerate it on each deploy.

findings.title: Tracking tags load with no consent tool in the page
findings.evidence: Google Tag Manager appears in the HTML and no consent platform or Google Consent Mode default was found. In the EU, the UK, Brazil, and Colombia this is a legal exposure.
findings.fix: Add a consent platform and set Google Consent Mode v2 defaults to denied before any tag loads.

findings.title: 1 page names another URL as canonical
findings.evidence: /download/releases/7.1/ → /download/releases/7-1. Search engines will usually index the other URL instead.
findings.fix: Make each page's canonical point at itself unless it is a real duplicate.

findings.title: Security headers on the start page are missing on other pages
findings.evidence: frame protection on 1 page, out of 20 pages read. Attackers pick the weakest page.
findings.fix: Set the headers once at the server, CDN, or host config so every response carries them.

findings.title: 1 cookie is sent without Secure
findings.evidence: Without Secure: old-theme.
findings.fix: Set Secure on every cookie, and HttpOnly plus SameSite=Lax on session cookies.

findings.title: 3 pages do not have exactly one h1
findings.evidence: /showcase/ (2), /patterns/ (2), /download/releases/7.1/ (0).
findings.fix: Give each page one h1 that names it.

findings.title: 2 titles run past about 60 characters
findings.evidence: /news/ (76), /five-for-the-future/ (97). Google cuts them with an ellipsis.
findings.fix: Lead with the words that matter and keep titles near 60 characters.

findings.title: 2 script hosts are loaded without integrity checks
findings.evidence: stats.wp.com, s.w.org. If that CDN is compromised, its code runs on the site.
findings.fix: Add integrity="sha384-…" and crossorigin="anonymous" to fixed-version CDN scripts.

findings.title: The Organization entity is incomplete
findings.evidence: 7 profiles linked on the page are not in sameAs (www.x.com, bsky.app, www.threads.net and 4 more).
findings.fix: Complete the entity so AI answers connect the brand to its profiles. The fix kit has a draft.

findings.title: HSTS max-age is shorter than six months
findings.evidence: max-age=3600.
findings.fix: Raise max-age to at least 15552000 (one year is 31536000).

findings.title: 1 page has no main landmark
findings.evidence: /gutenberg/.
findings.fix: Wrap the primary content in <main>.

findings.title: The start page sends no cache-control
findings.evidence: Browsers and CDNs guess how long to keep it.
findings.fix: Send cache-control on HTML (for example max-age=0, must-revalidate) and long max-age on hashed assets.

findings.title: Pages do not say who wrote them
findings.evidence: Author and date signals help search engines and AI answers judge whether a page is current and credible.
findings.fix: Show an author and a last-updated date on content pages, and add them to the JSON-LD.

findings.title: The start page took 864 ms to arrive
findings.evidence: Good sites deliver the HTML in under 800 ms.
findings.fix: Cache the HTML at the edge.

findings.title: 1 HTML document is heavier than 500 KB
findings.evidence: /gutenberg/ (1103 KB).
findings.fix: Move inline data and SVG out of the HTML.

findings.title: Core Web Vitals need improvement for real visitors
findings.evidence: Real Chrome users over the last 28 days on this page, at the 75th percentile: Largest Contentful Paint 2.9 s (needs improvement), Interaction to Next Paint 126 ms (good), Cumulative Layout Shift 0.01 (good). Source: Chrome UX Report through PageSpeed Insights.
findings.fix: Make the largest element arrive sooner: preload the hero image, serve it at the shown size in a modern format, and cut render-blocking scripts.

findings.title: Lighthouse scores performance 73/100 on mobile
findings.evidence: Lighthouse 13.5.0 on a simulated mid-range phone over slow 4G: Largest Contentful Paint 8.0 s, Total Blocking Time 89 ms, Cumulative Layout Shift 0, Speed Index 3.3 s.
findings.fix: Open PageSpeed Insights for this URL and work through its opportunities, largest savings first.

findings.title: 1 indexable page carries fewer than 150 words in the HTML
findings.evidence: /gutenberg/ (42 words).
findings.fix: Add useful copy, merge thin pages, or mark them noindex.

findings.title: Every internal link that was opened answered
findings.evidence: 19 linked pages answered without an error.

findings.title: Every page has a title
findings.evidence: 20 pages checked.

findings.title: Language alternates point at each other
findings.evidence: Every alternate that was read links back.

findings.title: Structured data parses and carries the expected properties
findings.evidence: Types: Organization, WebSite, WebPage, SoftwareApplication, Product.

findings.title: Share cards have a title, description, image, and URL
findings.evidence: og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url, and twitter:card are present.

findings.title: Unknown paths answer 404
findings.evidence: A made-up path answered 404.

findings.title: The start page sets a mobile viewport
findings.evidence: A viewport meta tag is present.

findings.title: AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page
findings.evidence: robots.txt does not block ChatGPT search, Claude, Perplexity, Google, or Bing at the root.

findings.title: The start page reads well without JavaScript
findings.evidence: 3382 characters of text are in the HTML.

findings.title: llms.txt is published
findings.evidence: /llms.txt has 9 sections and 36 links.

findings.title: A Organization entity names who is behind the site
findings.evidence: It is published on /.

findings.title: Some content is shaped as questions and answers
findings.evidence: 5 headings are phrased as a question.

findings.title: Pages show when they were published or changed
findings.evidence: A date was found on /.

findings.title: 1 measurement tool was found
findings.evidence: Google Tag Manager (GTM-P24PF4B).

findings.title: Campaign parameters survive the redirects
findings.evidence: A visit with utm_source, utm_medium, and utm_campaign kept them on /?utm_source=qa-lab-review&utm_medium=audit&utm_campaign=redirect-check.

findings.title: Plain http redirects permanently to https
findings.evidence: http:// answered 301 to https://wordpress.org/.

findings.title: Framing is limited
findings.evidence: X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN.

findings.title: The TLS certificate is valid for 64 more days
findings.evidence: Valid until 2026-12-22, issued by Let's Encrypt.

findings.title: security.txt tells researchers how to report a flaw
findings.evidence: /.well-known/security.txt has a Contact line.

findings.title: DMARC rejects or quarantines spoofed mail
findings.evidence: v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@automattic.com;.

findings.title: SPF is published
findings.evidence: v=spf1 ip4:66.6.42.0/24 ip4:66.155.40.0/24 include:helpscoutemail.com -all.

findings.title: The start page declares its language
findings.evidence: lang="en-US".

findings.title: Text contrast passes axe-core
findings.evidence: No contrast failure on 3 pages. Keyboard focus order still needs a person.

findings.title: axe-core found no WCAG 2.2 AA violation
findings.evidence: 3 rendered pages passed every automated rule. Automated rules catch about a third of real issues.

findings.title: The page fits a 390 px phone screen
findings.evidence: No sideways scroll in a phone-sized Chromium window.

findings.title: The page fits a 768 px tablet screen
findings.evidence: No sideways scroll at tablet width.

findings.title: The HTML carries the text people see
findings.evidence: The start page HTML holds 100% of the words on the rendered page.

findings.title: The largest element paints in 1.0 s
findings.evidence: Measured once in Chromium from an EU address (Belgium) with no network throttling. A phone on mobile data will be slower.

findings.title: The layout holds still while loading
findings.evidence: Cumulative Layout Shift 0.014. Measured once in Chromium from an EU address (Belgium) with no network throttling. A phone on mobile data will be slower.

findings.evidence: 50 requests on the start page.

cases.title: The reviewed URL answers over https
cases.why: The final URL was https://wordpress.org/ with status 200. A later run would open a real browser, keep the same host, and assert the step without submitting a form or generating load.

cases.title: The document has a title
cases.why: A title is present: Blog Tool, Publishing Platform, and CMS – WordPress.org. A later run would open a real browser, keep the same host, and assert the step without submitting a form or generating load.

cases.title: The document has one clear h1
cases.why: One h1 was found. Heading text would be compared with the visible hero, not only the tag count.

cases.title: The html element declares a language
cases.why: lang="en-US" is present. The declared language would be checked against the visible copy.

cases.title: Primary controls have an accessible name
cases.why: 7 button elements were counted. A later run would open a real browser, keep the same host, and assert the step without submitting a form or generating load. Empty buttons and icon-only controls would fail.

cases.title: Discovered pages keep a successful document status
cases.why: 20 saved pages stayed in the success range. A regression run would fail on a new 404 or 500 inside the same path list.

cases.title: Each saved page keeps a title
cases.why: Every saved page had a title. Titles would be asserted per path, including pages reached through one link.

cases.title: The meta description is present and short enough to read
cases.why: A description of 90 characters is present. The useful band for a snippet is about 50 to 160 characters.

cases.title: A canonical link points at the preferred URL
cases.why: Canonical is https://wordpress.org/. The preferred URL would be compared with the final https address of this read.

cases.title: Open Graph and Twitter cards describe the same page
cases.why: Open Graph tags are present. A Twitter card tag is present. A later case would assert og:title, og:image, and the card type.

cases.title: Structured data is valid when the page publishes it
cases.why: 1 JSON-LD block(s) were found. The type would be checked against the visible page, for example an organization, article, or product.

cases.title: The h1 and the title agree
cases.why: The first h1 is "Meet WordPress". The title and the h1 do not have to be identical, and they should not describe different pages.

cases.title: Same-host links discovered from the start page resolve
cases.why: 25 same-host links were listed. This review opened at most 20 of them and did not click them. A later run would request each href and accept only an HTML document on this host.

cases.title: The crawl stays inside the page cap and the host
cases.why: 20 HTML pages were saved, 2 links deep at most, with a cap of 20 pages. A regression would fail if a link left the host or if the cap stopped hiding a broken primary path.

cases.title: A crawler honors robots.txt for linked pages
cases.why: No linked URL was skipped for robots.txt during this read. The start URL is still fetched. A later crawler case would log each skipped path.

cases.title: Clicking “Showcase” opens /showcase/
cases.why: The start page navigation links “Showcase” to /showcase/ (header a[href="https://wordpress.org/showcase/"]). The page read there has the heading “Showcase”. A browser run would click the link at 1280 px, wait for /showcase/, and check the heading. Nothing is submitted.

cases.title: Clicking “Plugins” opens /plugins/
cases.why: The start page navigation links “Plugins” to /plugins/ (header a[href="https://wordpress.org/plugins/"]). The page read there has the heading “Plugins”. A browser run would click the link at 1280 px, wait for /plugins/, and check the heading. Nothing is submitted.

cases.title: Clicking “Themes” opens /themes/
cases.why: The start page navigation links “Themes” to /themes/ (header a[href="https://wordpress.org/themes/"]). The page read there has the heading “Themes”. A browser run would click the link at 1280 px, wait for /themes/, and check the heading. Nothing is submitted.

cases.title: Clicking “Hosting” opens /hosting/
cases.why: The start page navigation links “Hosting” to /hosting/ (header a[href="https://wordpress.org/hosting/"]). The page read there has the heading “Hosting”. A browser run would click the link at 1280 px, wait for /hosting/, and check the heading. Nothing is submitted.

cases.title: In-page anchors and repeated hrefs stay intentional
cases.why: Same-host hrefs were deduped before the crawl. A UI case would open repeated navigation items once and check that a hash target exists on the page.

cases.title: Visible fields have labels
cases.why: 1 form(s) are present. 0 controls had no label element, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title. Nothing was submitted. A later case would pair each control with its label.

cases.title: A later functional run uses a test account the owner provides
cases.why: Submitting the form is a different act from reading it. The account, the fixture data, and the expected confirmation stay outside this review.

cases.title: Required fields block an empty submit
cases.why: 1 inputs were marked required in the HTML. A browser case would submit the empty form and expect the constraint message, without creating a record.

cases.title: Search accepts a known term and an empty term
cases.why: A search control was detected in the HTML. The case would submit one known term and one empty term, and it would not scrape the result set.

cases.title: Images expose a text alternative
cases.why: 16 images, 8 without an alt attribute. Informative images need text. Decorative images need an empty alt.

cases.title: The page has a main landmark and a skip link
cases.why: A main element is present. A skip link was found. The review's headless browser runs axe-core on the rendered page.

cases.title: Heading order follows h1 then h2
cases.why: 1 h1 and 10 h2 elements were counted. The order would be checked in the rendered accessibility tree.

cases.title: Text contrast and keyboard focus are checked on the rendered page
cases.why: Contrast is measured by axe-core in the review's headless browser. Focus order still needs a person: the case would tab from the top of the page and record the focus ring.

cases.title: Frames expose a title
cases.why: 1 iframe(s), 1 without a title attribute. Each embedded document needs a name a screen reader can announce.

cases.title: HTTPS is the only way in
cases.why: The review refused any URL that was not https on port 443. A browser case would also request the http address and expect a redirect to https.

cases.title: HSTS is set
cases.why: strict-transport-security is present. The later assertion is max-age, includeSubDomains, and a fresh profile that stays on https.

cases.title: A content security policy is set
cases.why: content-security-policy was absent. The policy would be checked for script-src and frame-ancestors, not only for the header name.

cases.title: nosniff and a frame policy are set
cases.why: x-content-type-options: absent. x-frame-options: SAMEORIGIN. A framed copy of the page would be expected to fail when a frame policy is present.

cases.title: Referrer-Policy is set
cases.why: referrer-policy was absent. The later case would open an outbound link and confirm the referrer is no wider than the policy.

cases.title: Response headers do not need to reveal the server build
cases.why: Server header: nginx. The case records the header and does not treat a product name as a vulnerability by itself.

cases.title: A permissions policy limits powerful features
cases.why: No permissions-policy header was found. Camera, microphone, and geolocation would be expected to stay disabled unless the page needs them.

cases.title: The HTML does not reference plain http resources
cases.why: 0 scripts, images, frames, or stylesheets load over plain http. Mixed content would be confirmed in a browser console, not by downloading those URLs here.

cases.title: A privacy notice is linked from the page
cases.why: The HTML mentions a privacy or legal destination. Confirm the link in a browser before treating it as found.

cases.title: Third-party scripts are named before they run
cases.why: 1 other hosts were referenced by script src (stats.wp.com). A privacy case would load the page with tags blocked and then with consent.

cases.title: A consent notice is present when tags or cookies appear before a choice
cases.why: No cookie or consent wording was found. The case would assert the notice before analytics storage is written.

cases.title: Title, description, canonical, and social tags agree
cases.why: Title and description were read from the HTML. Open Graph tags would be asserted in a later browser case against the same final URL.

cases.title: Language alternates are explicit when the site has more than one language
cases.why: 157 hreflang alternate(s) were found. Each alternate would point at an https URL and include a self reference.

cases.title: A sitemap is advertised from the page or robots.txt
cases.why: No sitemap reference was seen in the HTML. The review fetches the sitemap from robots.txt or /sitemap.xml and compares it with the pages it read.

cases.title: AI answer and search crawlers may read the site
cases.why: robots.txt would be read for OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Claude-SearchBot, and Claude-User. A full Disallow for any of them keeps the site out of the answers that product writes. Training crawlers are a separate choice and are not asserted here.

cases.title: llms.txt lists the pages that matter, under a one-line summary
cases.why: The case fetches /llms.txt and expects a > summary line, the layout llmstxt.org proposes. It is a convention some AI tools read, not a ranking factor.

cases.title: The main heading and text are in the HTML before scripts run
cases.why: 524 words of text were in the served HTML. Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript, so they quote only what the server sends.

cases.title: An Organization or Person entity names who is behind the site
cases.why: A Organization entity is published in JSON-LD. AI answers use the entity to name the brand, its logo, and its profiles.

cases.title: Questions customers ask are answered under question headings or FAQ markup
cases.why: 0 heading(s) on the start page are phrased as a question. Answer engines favour a short answer under the question it answers.

cases.title: Content pages show when they were published or changed
cases.why: A published or modified date is present on the start page. No author is named, which the report lists separately. Search engines and AI answers weigh whether a page is current.

cases.title: The HTML document arrives inside a stated budget
cases.why: This read took 864 ms and 177653 bytes. That is one fetch, not a load test. A budget case would fail above 800 ms or 1.5 MB for the document alone. Lighthouse, through PageSpeed Insights, scores the rendered start page in the Performance findings.

cases.title: Script and stylesheet counts stay inside a budget
cases.why: 5 external scripts and 9 stylesheets were referenced. The later case would record the counts and the render-blocking ones.

cases.title: The slowest page in this read stays inside the same budget
cases.why: The slowest saved response was /plugins/ at 1120 ms. The trend across the crawl is the order the pages were opened, not a history of previous days.

cases.title: An authorised baseline could repeat the document fetch
cases.why: JMeter, Gatling, or k6 would need written permission, a verified domain, and a scheduled window. This review did not open a single virtual user. The baseline would be one request per second for a few minutes.

cases.title: A ramp would add users only inside an agreed ceiling
cases.why: The proposal is a short ramp, then a hold, then a stop. Error rate and response time would be the gates. No profile is generated by this review.

cases.title: A spike would last seconds, not an open-ended flood
cases.why: A spike case belongs on a staging host or a window the owner schedules. The public read here is still one document at a time.

cases.title: The layout holds at a phone width
cases.why: A viewport meta tag is present. Appium or Maestro would open a phone profile later and compare the same h1 and primary link.

cases.title: The same primary path works in a tablet width
cases.why: Width, orientation, and a touch scroll would be checked in Appium, Maestro, or a browser device profile. This HTML read did not resize a window.

cases.title: The lang attribute matches the copy a person reads
cases.why: Declared language: en-US. A bilingual page would need hreflang plus a visible language switch.

cases.title: Direction and locale formats stay with the language
cases.why: 157 alternate language links were counted. Dates, currency, and layout direction would be asserted only for locales the site claims.

cases.title: A missing path returns a deliberate not-found page
cases.why: This read did not save a 404. A later case would request one unknown path and expect a branded not-found document, not a stack trace.

cases.title: A slow document fails the case instead of hanging the suite
cases.why: This review stops a single page at 8 seconds. A suite would use its own timeout and a screenshot of the last frame.

cases.title: A repeat visit can reuse a cache policy the response already states
cases.why: No cache-control header was seen on the first response. The later case would record the header. It would not flush a shared cache.

cases.title: The page still explains itself when scripts do not run
cases.why: A noscript element is present. The case would disable JavaScript and check that the title and the main heading remain.

cases.title: The named stack is recorded with the case
cases.why: Markers seen in this read: WordPress, WooCommerce, Google Tag Manager, Google Fonts, nginx, React. The case list is filtered by the frameworks you select. Those tools are not launched. A later cross-browser pass could use BrowserStack. It is not started here.

cases.title: Analytics tags wait for a recorded choice when the page asks for consent
cases.why: An analytics marker was seen (WordPress, WooCommerce, Google Tag Manager, Google Fonts, nginx, React). The case would compare a cold load with a load after consent, and it would not invent a consent click.

cases.title: A catalog or payment marker is covered without placing an order
cases.why: A commerce or payment marker was seen (WordPress, WooCommerce, Google Tag Manager, Google Fonts, nginx, React). The case would open the public listing and stop before payment. No card data is entered.

cases.title: Images reserve their box before they paint
cases.why: 0 images had neither width nor height in the markup. Applitools or Percy would own a later visual diff. The review's headless browser measures layout shift on the start page.

cases.title: The first view stays inside the width the viewport asks for
cases.why: A viewport meta tag is present. The later case would open that width and look for a horizontal scroll on the main content.

cases.title: A robots meta tag matches the pages that should be indexed
cases.why: A robots meta tag is present. The later case would compare it with the canonical URL. This review does not submit the page to a search engine.

cases.title: A public API description is listed without calling the API
cases.why: The HTML mentions an API description. Postman could hold that collection later. This review did not send an API request.
